exam_name: SAFE MLO Test — State Component (various states)
passing_score_scale: Percentage (75% passing for all SAFE MLO test components)
exam_format: Linear (Pearson VUE in-person or OnVUE online proctored)
exam_price_notes: $69 USD in addition to the national component (UST); required in some states

testing_centers.notes: In-person testing at Pearson VUE test centers nationwide. Online proctoring available via Pearson VUE OnVUE.

id_requirements: Two forms of ID required at Pearson VUE test center: one government-issued photo ID with signature (primary) and one additional ID. Name on IDs must match NMLS registration exactly.
exam_rules: No personal items, notes, or reference materials permitted. Online proctored via Pearson VUE OnVUE: must be alone in room, no second monitors. Calculator provided on-screen; no personal calculators allowed. Candidates must complete NMLS-required pre-licensure education (PE) before scheduling. NMLS background check and credit report must be on file prior to testing.
renewal_options: MLO licenses are renewed annually through NMLS. 8 hours of continuing education (CE) required each year, including: 3 hours of federal law, 2 hours of ethics, 2 hours of non-traditional mortgage lending, and 1 hour of undefined instruction. State-specific CE may be required in addition to federal CE requirements. Renew at mortgage.nationwidelicensingsystem.org.

prerequisites.description: Must pass the national component (UST or NTP) before or concurrently with the state component. Required only in states that mandate a separate state component.

retake_policy.notes: 30-day waiting period after 1st and 2nd failed attempts. 180-day waiting period after 3rd and subsequent failed attempts. Each retake requires full exam fee ($110 or $69).

editorial.meta_description: The State-MLO exam is retired as of 2013-04-01. Review its domains and prepare for the verified successor, National Test with UST, to obtain your credentials.
editorial.overview: The SAFE MLO Test — State Component, certified by NMLS, covered state licensing laws, state mortgage laws, and state-specific regulatory requirements for aspiring mortgage professionals. This particular examination is officially retired as of 2013-04-01. Its verified successor is National Test with UST, which serves as the required replacement pathway for all candidates seeking proper licensing credentials today. Candidates must understand that this specific exam is no longer available for registration or completion, as the industry has transitioned to a unified testing model to ensure consistent standards across all jurisdictions for mortgage loan originators.
editorial.who_should_take: Individuals seeking mortgage loan originator licensing who must complete state-specific educational and testing requirements. Because this particular examination is retired, all candidates should pursue the National Test with UST instead to satisfy their professional licensing obligations.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Direct your preparation toward the National Test with UST rather than focusing on this retired examination format. Study current mortgage rules, detailed regulatory requirements, and statutory guidelines for state compliance to ensure familiarization with the required testing material before your exam date and schedule. Candidates should prioritize reviewing the official NMLS handbook to align their study habits with the current testing expectations and the 75% passing score requirement for all components.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Because this retired exam cannot be scheduled, candidates testing for current licensure take the successor exam via Pearson VUE in-person or OnVUE online proctored formats, ensuring they meet all modern testing protocols.

faq.answer_text: The established passing score is a percentage of 75% which is strictly required for all SAFE MLO test components to demonstrate adequate competency before receiving any professional mortgage licensing credentials in the industry.

faq.question_title: How much does the exam cost?
faq.answer_text: The price is $69 USD in addition to the national component known as UST, and this specific fee payment is required in some states for proper registration and processing of your licensing application.

The exam is officially retired as of 2013-04-01, with National Test with UST currently serving as the verified successor for all licensing candidates seeking to enter the mortgage industry and obtain professional credentials.

faq.question_title: What format is used for testing?
faq.answer_text: Testing follows a linear format administered through Pearson VUE in-person testing centers or convenient OnVUE online proctored options depending on the preference of the individual candidate seeking to complete their required mortgage certification.
